meta.title: The Rat Race
meta.description: Forty years, twenty rounds. Get rich, get status, get out.

guide.title: Guide
guide.news: Every round opens with the news. Each headline hints at the next two years, and not all of them come true. Read them before you put your money anywhere.
guide.cards: Life deals you a few cards every round. Each choice shows what it costs and what it brings before you pick, with the odds where there are dice. A choice cannot be taken back.
guide.finance: Now your money. Nothing here happens until you play the round, and the line above the button tells you, to the dollar, the cash you will have afterwards. Start in Portfolio.
guide.ledger: Two years went by. This is everything that came in and went out. Prices moved after you played, so what you own is worth something new.
guide.ratRace: The bar at the top is the whole game: your passive income against what your life costs. Cover the cost two rounds running and you are out of the rat race.
guide.invest: Cash earns nothing. Savings pay a little and are safe. To invest you need money sense 1: take a finance course (Lifestyle tab) or pay into the pension.
guide.focus: The Lifestyle tab holds your focus: study for a promotion, work overtime for pay now, or look for a better job. Use it every round.
guide.flow: Flow, at the top, is what you earn less what you spend in a year, before tax. The Taxes tab shows this round to the dollar.

news.title: News
news.hint: Headlines are about the next two years.
news.opener: The headlines beside this are about the next two years.

gossip.label: Opinion
gossip.0: Experts agree: this time is different
gossip.1: Twenty-somethings stop buying homes to buy avocados instead, says study
gossip.2: Man explains crypto at dinner; nobody asks a second question
gossip.3: Economist predicts nine of the last two recessions
gossip.4: Influencer quits job to live off passive income; sells course on it
gossip.5: "Property never goes down," says man who sells property
gossip.6: Survey: everyone is middle class, especially the rich
gossip.7: Bank raises fees to celebrate record profits

crisis.label: Crisis · year {year} of {of}
crisis.open: {crisis}: year {year} of {of}. See what it is.
crisis.advice: A crisis punishes whoever has to sell and whoever owes a lot. Those who hold usually get some of it back on the way out.
crisis.overHint: The world is back on its course. What fell does not rise by itself: see what you have left.

escape.title: Out of the rat race!
escape.body: At {age}, your income pays for your whole life without you. From today, work is a choice.
escape.hint: The earlier you get out, the bigger the bonus on your score. If your income stops covering your life, the wheel turns again.
escape.go: Carry on, for the fun of it

million.title: Your first million
million.body: At {age} you are worth a million real dollars: the kind that bought the same when you started.
million.hint: The second usually comes sooner than the first.

bankrupt.title: Bankrupt
bankrupt.body: At {age} your debts have beaten you. Everything you owned is sold and everything you owed is cancelled.
bankrupt.hint: No bank will lend to you until you are {age}. Your pension plan is untouched. Life goes on.

shop.sellGain: Sell it today and you gain {amount}

review.title: Reviews
review.1: "Not even the owner turns up here."
review.2: "You can tell they are losing money. Even the plant looks sad."
review.3: "Fine. The manager has no idea who the owner is."
review.4: "Good. I will be back if nothing else is open."
review.5: "The owner counts every penny, but everything works."

business.neglectedShort: Nobody runs it this round: it makes less and loses value.

evasion.title: What you do not declare
evasion.about: Paying the tax office less saves money now and draws suspicion. The more it suspects, the likelier an inspection.
evasion.blackHint: Part of your pay undeclared: you pay less income tax.
evasion.blackNoJob: Without a job there is no pay to take under the table.
evasion.shellHint: Saves {pct}% of the tax on your investments. A fee of {fee} a year.
evasion.cryptoHint: Gains on crypto pay no tax.
evasion.chance: Chance of an inspection when the round is played: {pct}%
evasion.bill: An inspection would cost {total}: {evaded} of tax, a {fine} fine and {goods} for what you bought without an invoice.
evasion.limit: What is hidden can be claimed for {years} years. An inspection also costs {status} status, and ends it all.

advisor.title: Your adviser
advisor.clean: "All in order. Frankly, a bit boring."
advisor.low: "That dinner, we will call it a business expense."
advisor.mid: "If anyone asks, the cash was a gift from an aunt. Do you have an aunt?"
advisor.high: "I would stop answering unknown numbers, if I were you."
advisor.max: "I have never met you. Who are you? Please leave."

resolve.title: Two years later
resolve.ledger: What came in and went out
resolve.jobHuntYes: The job hunt paid off: a lasting raise.
resolve.jobHuntNo: The job hunt led nowhere this time.
resolve.escaped: You are out of the rat race!
resolve.escapedHint: Your passive income covers your life. From here on, work is a choice.
resolve.escapeLostHint: Your passive income no longer covers your life. Cover it again and you are out again.
resolve.bankruptHint: Everything is sold and every debt is cleared. Banks will remember.
resolve.lapsedHint: It belonged to the city you left. Nothing is paid back.
resolve.movedRung: You start a rung down, until your next promotion.
resolve.movedPartner: Your partner is looking for work: a round without their pay.
resolve.planMissed: Your plan did not buy {name}: it needed {amount}.
resolve.marginCallHint: It fell too far for what you owed. It sold for {sold}, and {repaid} went to pay the loan.
resolve.marginCallShort: It fell too far for what you owed. It sold for {sold}, and you had to find another {short}.
resolve.businessClosedHint: There was nothing left in it.
resolve.auditHint: {evaded} of tax, a {fine} fine and {goods} for what you bought without an invoice. Nothing is hidden any more.

bank.title: Your bank
bank.card: "We have covered your shortfall with your credit card. No need to thank us. The interest will."
bank.idle: "We noticed a lot of money doing nothing. Our fund charges only 2% a year to do the same."
bank.fell: "We see your net worth has had a difficult couple of years. Have you considered a loan?"
bank.rich: "Your private banker would love a coffee. Your private banker is new, and likes you very much."

family.title: At the Christmas dinner
family.room: "Still in the room? Your cousin has a flat already. Two, actually."
family.frugal: Your mother slips a lunchbox into your bag. And another one.
family.car: Your brother-in-law asks what the car cost. Then asks again, in case it changed.
family.lavish: An aunt asks, very quietly, whether you won the lottery.
family.kids: The children open their presents in four minutes. The bill took you two years.
family.plain: Someone brings up politics. You leave before dessert.

profile.title: Your life
profile.leaveHint: Your life is saved after every step.
profile.itemWhen: It is sold or cancelled during the finances: here or in the Shop tab.
profile.itemUndo: It takes effect when the round is played. Until then you can take it out of the basket.
profile.aboutLifestyle: Your lifestyle multiplies what living costs you each year. Living on little shows and takes status away; the top two give it.
profile.aboutRent: Until you own a home in {city}, you rent. A room or a flat changes what you spend and your status.
profile.rentCost: The cost is that of your whole life with that rent, at the lifestyle you lead.
profile.aboutInsurance: You pay a premium every year. In return, when a bad card comes, the insurance pays part of the bill.
profile.changedIn: It is changed during the finances: here or in the Lifestyle tab.
profile.pickHere: Tap to choose. It takes effect when the round is played.

cash.title: Cash
cash.about: The money you have on hand. Your expenses, your purchases and your taxes come out of it.
cash.note: It earns nothing, and inflation eats it. Keep what the round needs and put the rest to work.

savings.title: Savings
savings.about: A deposit with no risk. It pays interest that follows the central bank's rate.
savings.note: If you ever run short of cash, the game takes it from here first, before it goes on the credit card.

pension.title: Pension plan
pension.about: Money put aside for the end. What you pay in lowers that round's tax.
pension.note: It cannot be touched before then, whatever happens. A bankruptcy does not take it either, and it counts in your net worth.

investments.title: Investments
investments.about: What you hold in the markets, at today's price.
investments.none: You have no investments yet. They are bought in the Market tab.
investments.note: The gain is over what you paid. When you sell, the taxman takes his share of it.

homes.title: Property
homes.about: Your properties, at what they are worth today. The mortgage on each is counted apart, under Debts.
homes.note: They are sold and let in the Property tab.

things.title: Things
things.about: What you own, at what you would get for it today. Tap one to look at it.
things.note: Nearly everything loses value each year. A few watches, bags and works of art hold it or gain.

debts.title: Debts
debts.about: Everything you owe. Each round you pay interest and repay a part.
debts.note: The credit card is the dearest and has no term: it fills by itself when cash runs short. Clear it first.

netWorth.title: Net worth
netWorth.about: Everything you own less everything you owe. It is half your score; the other half is status.

businesses.title: Businesses
businesses.about: What is in each of your businesses: what it is worth today.
businesses.note: They are run, grown and sold in the Business tab.

end.title: The end
end.statusHint: Status counts as you lived it: the average over the whole life.
end.never: You never left the rat race.
end.escapedAt: You left the rat race at {age}.
end.graph: Your net worth through life, after inflation
end.bankruptcies: {count, plural, =0 {Never bankrupt} one {Bankrupt once} other {Bankrupt # times}}
end.noBadges: No badge this time. The collection lists every one there is to earn.
end.compare: Better than {pct}% of the {life} lives others have played ({total}).

epilogue.title: Your life, told

opening.job: You started at {age} in {city}, as a {job}, with {cash} to your name.
opening.none: You started at {age} in {city}, with no job and {cash} to your name.

epilogue.quiet: It was a quiet life: no moves, no shocks and no big bets. Year after year, the same, and on time.

obituary.title: Obituary
obituary.cars: Leaves {n} cars and nobody to drive them.
obituary.things: Leaves more things than money, and a cupboard that will not close.
obituary.miser: Died rich, without ever once turning on the heating.
obituary.room: Leaves a room in a shared flat, and a deposit nobody will give back.
obituary.free: Worked less than anyone, and was never once in a hurry.
obituary.broke: Owed money to people who no longer remember the name.
obituary.heirs: Leaves a fortune, and a family that will argue over it for years.
obituary.alone: Leaves a fortune, and nobody to argue over it.
obituary.plain: Paid every bill on time. Nobody mentions it.

work.title: Work
work.noJobSub: You live on what you have
work.top: At the top of your career. Career skill {skill}.
work.focusRested: +{n} from the rest your trip gave you
work.careerAbout: A career in {career}. Each round worked gives +{work} career skill, and studying +{study} more. When you reach the skill a job asks for, you are promoted.
work.noJobAbout: You have no job on a career ladder. Some cards open one; until then you live on your income and on what you own.
work.ladderNote: Pay in {city} today, with the raises and cuts you already carry.
work.financeAbout: It says which investments you can buy on your own. Nothing you already hold is lost for lacking the level.

financeOpens.0: Nothing yet: savings and the pension only. A finance course opens level 1.
financeOpens.1: Index funds, bonds, stocks and gold: {n} to choose from.
financeOpens.3: No new market: what changes is whose money you buy with.

work.financeHow: Each round with money invested gives +{n}. A course or a good book takes you up a level, as far as 2: level 3 comes only from investing.
work.focusAbout: Focus is your time and your energy for two years. This round you have {total}.
work.focusBonus: {n} is from the rest your last trip gave you.
work.focusNoJob: Without a job there is no overtime, no career study and no job hunt: focus is left for learning, for moving and for the cards.
work.studyGives: +{n} career skill, on top of what working gives.
work.huntGives: {pct}% chance of a {raise}% raise for good.
work.focusAlso: Moving city takes 1 focus, and some cards ask for 1 or 2 to take their best option.
work.focusWhere: It is spent in the Lifestyle tab, during the finances.
work.cycleUp: Your pay follows the economy: this round you earn {pct}% more.
work.cycleDown: Your pay follows the economy: this round you earn {pct}% less.
work.cycleFlat: Your pay follows the economy: up in good times, down in bad. This round, neither.
work.fadeLater: It is a trade for the young: from the age of {age} you earn {pct}% less each round, down to {max}% less.
work.fadeNow: Your audience is growing up: this round you earn {pct}% less, and it will fall to {max}%.
work.jobFocus: It leaves time over: +{n} focus every round.
work.focusJob: +{n} because your job leaves time over
work.focusFromJob: {n} comes from your job, which leaves time over.
work.financeMargin: And buying with money borrowed from the broker.
work.skillLiving: You already practise it: +{n} a round.
work.financeIdle: You have nothing invested right now, so nothing adds up.

skillHow.negotiation: Job hunting, or working in sales, law or finance: +{n} a round.
skillHow.languages: Living away from your home city, or working in hospitality: +{n} a round.
skillHow.network: Belonging to a club, or working in sales, social media, hospitality or public service: +{n} a round.
skillHow.management: Only by running a business: +{study} a round if you run it, +{n} with a manager.
skillHow.health: Going to the gym, or working in healthcare or medicine: +{n} a round.
